subject: Problem with posterior 'mean' and 'sd' of the GMRF

messages.author: e5c7e56038437512
messages.subject: Problem with posterior 'mean' and 'sd' of the GMRF
parts:
Hi!

I hope you are well!
I have a problem to predict the distribution of the mean and sd for the spatial random effect in a spatio-temporal model. The spatial effect was incorporated through the 'spde' method and the response variable was modelled with a joint likelihood (binomial and zero-inflated negative binomial). 


The problem is the following: the mesh is bounded (left side in 'plot1' attached) to estimate only inside of the spatial domain determined by the limits but the 'mean' (center) and the 'sd' (right side) are out of those limits (specifically on the right side), for the above my question.
¿Why the prediction of the 'mean' and 'sd' could be out of that limits? 


The right side is 'land' because it corresponds to Argentina and the left side corresponds to the ocean Pacific. The map is south of Chile. 


Beforehand thank you very much

Best regards!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with posterior 'mean' and 'sd' of the GMRF
parts:
Hi,
you've defined the mesh and model so that it's defined on a region larger than the domain of interest.
This is good, in the sense that it moves SPDE boundary effects away from the region of interest.
If you're only interested in the results over land, then you can simply mask out the points that are over land (I'm guessing from the plots that the are of interest is the ocean, but it's not entirely clear); in the plot, you've calculated the result on a grid that only covers part of the mesh, and what you need to do is just to remove all the points on land.

The benefit of the above approach is that it's easy.
If you need a model that isn't spatially stationary and isotropic, but rather takes into account the complicated archipelago geometry, then you'll want to use the "barrier model" approach, that prohibits dependence across land (if the model is to live on the ocean), see http://www.r-inla.org/barrier-model
For those models, you also need to filter out the locations outside the domain of interest.

Finn

Best regards.
